disagreements.topic: Cost of owned sites: facility capex per MW and running cost (the largest swing in round 4)
disagreements.positions: Facility capex per gross MW, on top of IT: agent_5 $7.5M, agent_1 $10M, agent_4 ~$11M (owned capex 114% of a $25M unit = $28.5M all-in incl. $17.5M IT), agent_3 $12M, agent_2 $16M (+2.5%/yr maintenance; $36.25M all-in). Running cost for owned sites (power + site O&M): agent_4 $1.1M, agent_1 $1.2M, agent_3 $1.3M plus $0.6M/yr facility sustaining capex, agent_5 $1.5M (incl. ~$0.5M network that leased MW also pay), agent_2 power $0.8M plus 2.5% maintenance (site ops inside its company-wide $2.35M 'other fixed'). What the F2 fix added to each DCF: agent_3 +$1, agent_1 +$12.5, agent_2 +$30 net (+$50 cost split, -$20 maintenance), agent_4 +$44, agent_5 +$77. The note's '$10-28.5M' mixes facility-only and all-in figures: facility-only runs $7.5-16M, and $28.5M is agent_4's all-in owned capex.
disagreements.resolution: Settled at $13M of facility capex per gross (utility) MW (range $12-14M), plus $1.2M/MW-yr of power and site O&M and ~$0.26M/MW-yr of facility sustaining capex (2% of facility cost), about $1.45M/MW-yr all-in. Nebius quotes its campuses in utility MW (Independence: '1.2 GW sized facility, 800 MW from IPL and 400 MW on-site generation'), so per-IT-MW benchmarks are converted at PUE ~1.3. The evidence: C&W 2026 puts all-in greenfield cost excluding chips at $17.6M/MW on average ($8.9-23.3M range), which is ~$13.5M per utility MW. JLL's 2026 shell-and-core figure is $11.3M/MW, a floor because it leaves out liquid-cooling fit-out. B. Riley estimates Applied Digital's Polaris Forge 2 at ~$12M/MW. agent_5's $7.5M sits below the C&W range even on an IT-MW basis, and below JLL's shell alone. agent_2's $16M plus 2.5%/yr maintenance is at the top, and agent_3's $0.6M/yr sustaining (~5% of facility cost a year) is high. I applied the settled costs to every agent using its own sensitivities. Where an agent gave no running-cost sensitivity, I built one bottom-up from its expected owned MW: adjusted split DCFs agent_1 ~$122 (from $144), agent_2 ~$149 (from $121), agent_3 ~$105 (from $97), agent_4 ~$171 (from $188), agent_5 ~$132 (from $178). The range narrows from $97-188 to ~$105-171.
disagreements.evidence: Cushman & Wakefield 2026 Data Center Development Cost Guide PR (3 Sep 2026); JLL 2026 Global Data Center Outlook; Archdesk/B. Riley on Polaris Forge 2; nebius.com/independencemo (fetched 2 Oct 2026); agent sensitivities (agent_1 facility $8.5M/$12M -> $153/$134; agent_2 $12M/$25M -> $148/$50; agent_3 $10M/$13.5M -> $122/$78; agent_4 owned capex 130% of unit -> $163, owned cost $1.6M -> $164; agent_5 facility $10M -> $161, owned fixed $2.0M -> $156).

disagreements.topic: Where the Meta orders sit, and at what $/MW
disagreements.positions: Meta-2025 ($2.9B): agents 1 and 4 put it on 48-50 MW of Mantsala 1; agents 2, 3 and 5 spread ~48-50 MW pro rata over the energized non-Vineland fleet. All price it at ~$11.6-12M/MW. Meta $12B dedicated: agent_1 160 MW at $15M (MAN2 70 + LPR 90); agent_2 133 MW at $18M (MAN2 70 + LPR 63); agent_3 130 MW at ~$18.5M (MAN2 70 + LPR 60); agent_4 150 MW at $16M (MAN2 70 + LPR 80); agent_5 172 MW at $14M (MAN2 70, LPR 50, Harlow 22, Birmingham 30). Backstop (up to $15B): agent_1 200 MW at Birmingham, floor $15M/MW at 100% (9.0%); agent_2 167 MW at Birmingham, floor $18M, revenue = max(market, floor) (8.5%); agent_3 150 MW at Highridge, $13.5B floor (8.75%); agent_4 190 MW at Lappeenranta, 85% of $16.5M (9.5%); agent_5 214 MW at Highridge, $14M floor (8.5%).
disagreements.resolution: No double counting within any agent: each site's MW add up to its inventory envelope. The Meta press release and 6-K disclose no MW, sites or backstop prices, so every mapping is judgment, and location matters only through ownership (cost) and timing. The value-relevant choice is $/MW, because MW = $2.4B/yr divided by price, and capex scales with MW. Vera Rubin capex per MW is above Blackwell's, so $16-18M/MW (130-150 MW) is better supported than agent_5's $14M (172 MW) or agent_1's $15M. The effect is small: agent_1 gives $141/$149 at $12M/$20M, agent_5 $176/$181 at $12M/$16M. All five correctly treat the backstop as Meta's obligation to buy unsold capacity: a put held by Nebius, with Meta paying Nebius. It is worth only ~$0.2-2.5/share on top of market pricing. Reconciled convention: Meta-2025 pro rata on the existing fleet; dedicated on 2027 owned Finnish builds (MAN2 + first LPR phase) at ~$16-18M/MW; backstop on the first owned US phase (Birmingham or Highridge 260 MW), floored at the pre-agreed price and capped at $15B in total.
disagreements.evidence: Nebius newsroom, 'Nebius signs new AI infrastructure agreement with Meta' (16 Mar 2026): five-year term, $12B dedicated 'across multiple locations', Vera Rubin, deliveries from early 2027, Meta to buy up to $15B of available capacity on certain upcoming clusters; no MW or sites disclosed. CNBC 16 Mar 2026.

disagreements.topic: The ~1 GW of contracted power with no named site (5 GW YE26 target less ~3.95 GW named)
disagreements.positions: agent_1 leaves it out (upside; Oklahoma 50 MW only). agent_2 leaves it out (Oklahoma 100 MW only). agent_3: Oklahoma 100 MW plus 900 MW unallocated, p 0.5, owned economics 2029-31 ($5.0/sh). agent_4: Oklahoma 300 MW plus a 700 MW gap layer, p 0.5, owned-cost merchant 2029-31 ($9.6/sh). agent_5: one 1,050 MW bucket that includes Oklahoma and any Vineland Phase 2, p 0.4, leased costs 2030-32 ($9.4/sh).
disagreements.resolution: Agents 3-5 account for it once, without double counting Oklahoma or Vineland Phase 2. Agents 1-2 drop it, which conflicts with the brief's rule that pipeline be probability-weighted rather than omitted. 5 GW is a YE26 contracted-power target, not a signed fact, and no site, owner or date is disclosed. The consistent treatment is p ~0.4-0.5, energizing 2029-31, net of build capex at the settled owned costs, discounted at WACC. At those costs it is worth ~$4-8/share. I add ~+$4 (agent_1) and ~+$5 (agent_2).
disagreements.evidence: sites.md summary (5 GW target vs ~3.95 GW named; US-OK MW undisclosed); agent site_coverage rows.

disagreements.topic: Contract discount rates and split vs single-rate DCF
disagreements.positions: Investment-grade contract-term rates: agent_1 7.5-9.0% (PV-weighted 7.8%), agent_2 8.5%, agent_3 8.0/8.75%, agent_4 8.5% (backstop 9.5%), agent_5 7.5/8.5%. Unrated Q2-26 deals 10.0-11.0%. WACC 12.0-12.8% on post-contract, uncontracted, pipeline and terminal cash flows. Split adds +$3 to +$4.6 in every model (single/split: $140/$144, $118/$121, $93/$97, $184/$188, $175/$178).
disagreements.resolution: Sound in every agent. All anchor on the $775M secured facility at SOFR+2.50%, which I verified (Business Wire 17 Jul 2026; matures 31 Oct 2030; backed by an IG customer's contracted cash flows). SOFR was 3.87% on 1 Oct and the 5-yr UST 5.01% (5.09% on 30 Sep), also verified. That gives ~6.4% floating or ~7.5% fixed-equivalent. The 0-150bp premiums added for delivery and termination risk and the unfinanced slice are reasonable, and Meta's 4.55% 2031 notes are a valid pure-credit floor. Every agent applies the contract rate only inside signed terms, to cash flows net of opex, tax and build capex. The split matters little because the contracts are short and the Meta builds absorb early cash: ~$29-60/share of contracted value against DCFs of $97-188. One methodological caveat, flagged by agent_3 itself: carving low-risk flows out of a firm-level beta leaves a riskier residual. At a 13.1% residual rate, agent_3's split DCF is $75, so split-rate DCFs are a slight upper bound.
disagreements.evidence: Business Wire / SEC 6-K ex99-1 (17 Jul 2026); NY Fed SOFR API (3.87% on 2026-10-01); US Treasury daily par yield curve (5-yr 5.01%, 10-yr 5.24% on 2026-10-01).

disagreements.positions: All five value all 25 inventory sites exactly once. Energized and contracted capacity carries its contract terms, and under-construction and pipeline capacity is probability-weighted (0.5-0.95) net of capex. Vineland is 300 MW everywhere, Bethune is treated as leased everywhere, and Microsoft runs to ~mid-2031 everywhere. Payment direction is correct in all five: Microsoft and Meta pay Nebius; Nebius pays DataOne, Kao, AIB, Mega Or and Azur. No sold sites (none exist), and no power counted twice (Palantir given $0 by all; Vineland Phase 2 excluded or held inside the unnamed bucket).
disagreements.resolution: No disagreement with the inventory needed a primary-source check: no agent disputed an inventory fact. I re-verified the facts my verdict rests on (Meta terms, $775M facility, Independence MW basis). Residual small issues: (i) agents 2-5 apply gross-MW revenue rates to IT-MW figures at leased IT-only sites (Harlow, Beit Shemesh, Masmiya, Estonia, Madrid, AIB; ~200 MW), while agent_1 converts them at 1.3x. The effect is under ~$2/share. (ii) Undisclosed MW (Longcross 13-20, Modi'in 5-10, Woodbury 5-10, Newport/UK-4th 12-16, Oklahoma 50-300) are judgment and immaterial except Oklahoma, which agents 3-5 tie to the unnamed-GW bucket.
disagreements.evidence: Agent site_coverage tables checked row by row against sites.md and sites.json.

disagreements.positions: All: unannounced, likely mid-November, outside the window.
disagreements.resolution: Still 'No upcoming events yet' on 2 Oct 2026. The last events were the Citi and Goldman conferences on 8-9 Sep and the Q2 results on 12 Aug. I keep the forecasters' 1-month mean.

one_month_reasoning: I kept the forecasters' 1-month mean (P>=spot 0.488): the Q3 date is still unannounced (likely mid-November), and the round-4 site and discount-rate work changes long-run value, not the October event set (hyperscaler capex prints, ATM supply, rates).
confidence_reason: The settled owned-site cost narrows the DCF range from $97-188 to ~$105-171 and lowers the reconciled DCF mean from $146 to ~$136. But DCFs carry only 40-50% of each blend, so the restated fair-value mean moves just -$5 (~$195 to ~$190). My ladder trims the mean by about 1 point in the middle (P>=$232 0.452 -> 0.442), undoing part of agents 4-5's round-4 rise, which rested mostly on the low owned-site costs. That does not clearly change the distribution, so the mean should stand.
thesis_break_reason: Four agents sit at $115 and agent_4 at $120. $115 is below the $138.75 Sep-25 conversion price and near the low end of the reconciled DCFs at a 5-year life or steep re-lease path. A close there would most likely mean new-deal $/MW reverting toward the ~$12M fleet base, owned campuses (Highridge 260 MW by Oct-2027, Meta tranches from early 2027) slipping, or contract-secured financing failing to scale. Ordinary volatility is unlikely to explain it. The signed IG contracts (~$29-60/share net of build capex) are the floor beneath it.
key_drivers: Revenue per MW over a cohort's life (new-cohort price, the 5-year share, the re-lease path) is still the biggest lever: agent_3 launch price +/-$2M/MW gives $26-167; agent_2 glut vs supply-short gives $50-199; agent_5 relaunch $16M/$20M gives $131-225.

Owned-site economics, now settled at ~$13M facility capex per utility MW and ~$1.45M/MW-yr all-in running cost (C&W 2026 $17.6M/IT-MW excl. chips; JLL $11.3M shell-and-core). Each $1M/MW of facility cost moves the DCFs $5-13/share, and each $0.1M/MW-yr of running cost moves them ~$4-5. Owned sites hold ~3.1 GW, ~70-75% of expected MW.

Contract book: Microsoft $17.4B to mid-2031, Meta $2.9B plus $12B dedicated from early 2027, the backstop up to $15B, and Q2-26 deals over $4B. It is worth ~$29-60/share net of build capex at 7.5-9.0% (anchored on the SOFR+2.50% facility). The split rate adds only $3-5 because the terms are short.

Execution and funding of >1 GW/yr: Highridge 260 MW by Oct-2027, Independence additional power by early 2029, Birmingham lawsuits, the ~1 GW of the 5 GW target with no named site, and dilution toward ~380-400M shares.
The sector multiple (CoreWeave ~4-5x EV/NTM sales, ~8-9x forward EBITDA) carries 50-60% of every blended fair value.

fair_value.reason: Agents' round-4 fair values are $190/$198/$159/$228/$198 (mean $194.5). Restated with the settled owned-site costs and the unnamed-GW treatment applied to each agent's DCF leg at its own weight, plus the net-debt effect of the changed facility capex on its multiples legs: agent_1 ~$178 (DCF $122, EV/sales ~$215), agent_2 ~$214 (DCF $149, EV/EBITDA ~$280), agent_3 ~$161 (DCF $105), agent_4 ~$218 (DCF $171, multiples -$3), agent_5 ~$176 (DCF $132, EV/sales ~$205). Mean ~$190, ~18% below spot. Reconciled DCFs alone: split ~$105-171 (mean ~$136), single ~$101-166 (mean ~$132).

missed: Owned facility capex of $10M per utility MW is below the evidence: C&W 2026 puts the average at $17.6M per MW excluding chips (~$13.5M per utility MW at PUE 1.3), and JLL's shell-and-core alone is $11.3M. At $13M your split DCF is ~$128.
You carry no facility sustaining capex ('the owned facility is not rebuilt'). About 2%/yr of facility cost (~$0.26M/MW-yr) takes off ~$10.
You exclude the ~1 GW of contracted power with no named site entirely. The brief asks for pipeline to be probability-weighted, not omitted: at p ~0.45 for 2029-31 it adds ~+$4.
feedback_for_agents.revisit: Rerun at $13M facility, $1.2M opex plus $0.26M sustaining, and include the unnamed GW (reconciled split DCF ~$122). Consider pricing Meta's Rubin capacity at $16-18M/MW rather than $15M.

missed: Your $16M facility plus 2.5%/yr maintenance sits at the top of the evidence. JLL's $11.3M plus $4.5-5.2M of liquid cooling double-counts part of the C&W all-in figure, which already includes MEP. At $13M your DCF is ~+$22.
Like agent_1, you leave out the ~1 GW of contracted power with no named site (~+$5 at p ~0.45).
feedback_for_agents.revisit: Use ~$13M facility with ~2%/yr sustaining. Show owned site O&M separately from the company-wide $2.35M 'other fixed' so the owned/leased gap is explicit. Reconciled split DCF ~$149.

missed: Facility $12M is close to the evidence ($13M settled), but the $0.6M/MW-yr sustaining capex is ~5% of facility cost a year, roughly double typical M&E replacement. At ~2% (~$0.26M) your DCF gains ~+$20.
Your facility sensitivity (~$12.6/share per $1M/MW) is about twice the other agents', because the converts are treated as debt on 322M shares. Say so when comparing.
feedback_for_agents.revisit: Reconciled split DCF ~$105 (single ~$101); still below both conversion prices, so treating the converts as debt stays consistent.

Lappeenranta carrying both the Meta dedicated tranche (80 MW) and the backstop (190 MW) by mid-2028 assumes a fast phased build on a site that only says 'first capacity 2027'. The value effect is small but the timing is aggressive.
feedback_for_agents.revisit: Reconciled split DCF ~$171. The owned-cost change (F2, +$44) is your largest change since round 3, so keep the 130%-of-unit case visible.

missed: Owned facility capex of $7.5M/MW is below every source: under the C&W range even per IT MW ($8.9-23.3M, avg $17.6M) and under JLL's shell-and-core alone ($11.3M). This is why your F2 fix is worth +$77. At $13M your split DCF is ~$132, not $178.
Your owned running cost of $1.5M includes ~$0.5M of network, so site cost is only ~$1.0M; power plus site O&M is ~$1.2M.
Meta dedicated at $14M/MW (172 MW) under-prices Rubin capacity relative to its capex.

summary: Round 4 rebuilt every DCF from the 25-site inventory with split discounting. All five agents account for each site once with correct terms and payment direction, and anchor contract rates soundly on the verified SOFR+2.50% facility (7.5-9.0% investment-grade, at WACC outside the terms). The split adds only $3-5 because the contracts are short. The big swing was the cost of owned campuses: facility capex ranged from $7.5M to $16M per MW, worth +$1 to +$77 per agent. Settling it at ~$13M per utility MW (C&W 2026, JLL) and ~$1.45M/MW-yr all-in narrows the DCFs from $97-188 to ~$105-171 (single-rate ~$101-166). The restated fair value is ~$190, ~18% below spot. The ladder is trimmed by ~1 point (P>=$232 0.442), with low confidence.

sizing.conviction_label_reason: My checks found no expected-return edge over the S&P 500 per unit of risk: the reconciled fair value (~$190) and the ladder median (~$215) sit below spot, and ~100% volatility sets a high Sharpe hurdle.
sizing.entry: 2 tranches: half after the late-October hyperscaler capex prints, half after the Q3 report and formal 2027 guide (likely mid-November)
sizing.overlap: AVGO and GOOGL (AI-capex cycle; Google is both a neocloud customer and a competitor) and VST (AI data-center power demand). About 14% of the portfolio already rides AI-infrastructure spend.
sizing.reason: To beat SPY's Sharpe at ~100% realized volatility, NBIS needs roughly a +45-50% return, which the ladder puts at ~0.22-0.25 probability. It shares the AI-capex driver with AVGO, GOOGL and VST and carries dilution, financing and Q3-guide event risk. A 2% cap holds a thesis-break loss (~-50%) to about 1% of the portfolio.
